name: Corrective EQ (8-band)
purpose: Clean, transparent 8-band corrective EQ (LSP Parametric Equalizer, minimum-phase IIR): high-pass and low-pass filters, notches for hum or resonances, and surgical cuts for boxiness, mud and harshness. Use it for cleanup BEFORE console_eq, which is the character EQ for colour and broad tone shaping.

params.name: Output gain
params.ai_hint: Compensate for large boosts or cuts so the module's output level matches its input. Usually leave at 0.

params.name: Filter type 0
params.ai_hint: Leave unused bands Off. Use Hi-pass on band 0 to remove rumble below the source's lowest useful note.

params.name: Frequency 0
params.ai_hint: Centre or corner frequency in Hz.

params.name: Gain 0
params.ai_hint: Bell and shelf bands only (ignored by pass and notch). Prefer cuts of 2-6 dB; boosts rarely above 3 dB.

params.name: Quality factor 0
params.ai_hint: Higher is narrower: 0.7 broad, 2-4 targeted cuts, 8+ notches and hum. Use 0.4 for Hi-pass and Lo-pass (flat, no resonance).

params.name: Filter slope 0
params.ai_hint: Steepness for pass and shelf filters: x1 gentle (12 dB/oct) to x4 steep.

hidden_params.reason: Equaliser mode (always zero-latency IIR; FIR, FFT and spectral modes cost CPU and add latency), per-band filter mode (always RLC), width, input gain and analyser controls stay at defaults.

notes: LSP stores gains as linear amplitude; Plugsalot converts from dB (convert = db_to_amp).

The module runs the vendored LSP Filter class per band in IIR mode with LSP's own RLC filter mapping. Upstream Q is a damping factor (2 / (1 + Q)), so it is not identical to a textbook Q; Plugsalot always sends an explicit Q.
